newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Kredietbank staff questioned by court in tax probe.
newsitem.headline: Kredietbank staff questioned by court in tax probe.

text.p: Staff members of Kredietbank NV, one of Belgium's top four banks, are currently being questioned by the Belgian judicial police in a bank tax fraud probe, a spokeswoman for the bank said on Monday.

"The judicial police is at this moment questioning staff members of our fiscal department. We do not know what this is about, it may have something to do with a bourse operations tax case or with our Luxembourg sister bank Kredietbank Luxembourg," the spokeswoman for Kredietbank told Reuters.
Kredietbank has been under fire in recent weeks in Belgian media over allegations of tax evasion.
One case involves the so-called flat-rate tax on income from foreign investments.

In the late eighties, coupons on bonds from certain countries gave right to a flat-rate tax break, even if no taxes had been paid abroad. Belgian media have said banks also passed on benefits from this tax loophole to their corporate clients. The Belgian tax authorities are now allegedly reclaiming bourse tax on the securities sold in this framework.
Kredietbank Luxembourg, Kredietbank's sister bank, has been the object of an investigation into tax avoidance since last year.
Earlier on Monday, the offices of Belgian Finance Minister Philippe Maystadt were searched by judicial police probing tax fraud.
Belgian media have reported that Maystadt had intervened with the tax administration in favour of Kredietbank. Maystadt has denied any wrongdoing.
It was not immediately clear whether there is a link between Monday's two court actions.
-- Geert De Clercq, Brussels Newsroom +32 2 287 6813, Fax +32 2 230 7710
